notes: Variant assumption: standing high-cable straight-arm pulldown using a bar or rope, with elbows nearly fixed and the handle pulled toward the thighs. Muyor et al. directly supports latissimus dorsi as primary and triceps brachii as a meaningful secondary contributor. Teres major is included only as explicit inference from related pulldown-family EMG and shoulder-extension/adduction mechanics because the exact straight-arm pulldown study did not measure teres major. Middle/lower trapezius support comes from isometric pulldown angle evidence. Pectoralis major and rectus abdominis were measured in the direct study but were not added as visible roles because the straight-arm cable pulldown is more cleanly represented as a lat/triceps/scapular-support movement. Local anatomy mesh mappings resolve for all visible muscles.
